# Simple Floorplan

> Simple Floorplan is a 2D apartment floorplan editor that runs in the browser. It has two modes, Plan and Design. The document format is ProjectDoc schemaVersion 3. All units are centimetres (cm) and degrees. The x axis points right and the y axis points down.

## What the app is

- Web app (React and SVG), installable as a PWA, works offline. Projects are saved in the browser (IndexedDB).
- Optional cloud sync: project documents are stored in Cloudflare D1, images in Cloudflare R2. Both are reached through the Worker API below.
- A project is one ProjectDoc (schemaVersion 3). It holds `refImages` and one or more `artboards`. An artboard holds `rooms`, `openings` and `furniture`.
- Room: a polygon of `vertices` (interior). Walls are drawn outward from each edge. Each wall has an edge index.
- Wall kind: `wallKinds` maps an edge index as a string (`"0"`, `"1"`, ...) to `"wall"` or `"fence"`. A fence is a low railing, for example a balcony parapet, about 100 cm high and 4 cm thick. An edge with no entry is a normal wall.
- Opening: a door, window or opening (`kind`) placed on a wall, with a centre (`xCm`, `yCm`), an `angleDeg`, a `widthCm` and optional style `variant`.
- Furniture: a `rect` or `circle` item with a position, size, `rotationDeg` and `color`.
- Reference image: a PNG, JPG, WebP, SVG or PDF placed on the plan (Plan mode only), with `cmPerPx` scale and `opacity`.
- Modes: Plan (key `1`) and Design (key `2`). In Design mode the furniture panel and the tape tool are used.
- Export: artboard SVG, PNG, and the project as JSON (file, or Copy JSON / Copy SVG). Import: a project JSON file, or Paste JSON. Older v1 JSON exports are converted on import.

## Machine-readable specs (no token needed)

- `GET /api/openapi.json`: OpenAPI 3.1.0 document for the whole Worker API.
- `GET /api/schema/project.v3.json`: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for ProjectDoc schemaVersion 3.

Both responses use `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`.

## REST API (Cloudflare Worker)

Source: `functions/worker.ts` (routes, auth, docs) and `functions/mcp.ts` (MCP endpoint). All routes are under `/api/` on the same host as the app. Locally, `npm run dev:api` (build, then `npx wrangler dev --port 8788`) serves the API on `http://localhost:8788`. The Vite dev server (`npm run dev`) proxies `/api` to `http://localhost:8788`, so run the Worker on that port in a second terminal.

D1 migrations: `migrations/0001_projects.sql` (the projects table) and `migrations/0002_version_and_tokens.sql` (the `version` column and the `api_tokens` table). Local: `npm run db:migrate:local`. Remote: `npm run db:migrate:remote`.

### Authentication

Send one of these headers:

- `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The token is a scoped token (`sfp_...`) or the master secret.
- `x-api-token: <secret>`. The value is the master secret or a scoped token.

The master secret is the Worker secret `PASSCODE` (checked first) or `API_TOKEN`. It has the `admin` scope on every project. Set it with `npx wrangler secret put PASSCODE`.

Scoped tokens come from `POST /api/tokens` (admin only). Each token has:

- `scopes`: `read` < `edit` < `admin`. Default `read`.
- `projectId` (optional): the token works on this one project only.

Scope needed per route:

- `read`: `GET /api/projects`, `GET /api/projects/:id`, `POST /api/projects/:id/query`, `GET /api/projects/:id/render.svg`, `GET /api/images/...`.
- `edit`: `POST /api/projects`, `PUT`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/projects/:id`, `POST /api/projects/:id/commands`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/images/...`.
- `admin`: all `/api/tokens` routes.
- `POST /api/mcp`: `read` to enter. Each MCP tool checks its own scope (see the MCP section).

Errors:

- `401 {"error":"Unauthorized"}`: credentials are missing or wrong. If neither secret is set, the API is open (admin), unless the request sends a Bearer token that is not a known token.
- `403 {"error":"Forbidden"}`: the scope is too low, or the token is limited to another project.
- Only the two discovery routes skip the token check when a secret is set.
- The web app keeps the master value in browser local storage under the key `sfp-cloud-token` and sends it as `x-api-token`.

### Discovery (no token)

| Method | Path | Result |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/openapi.json` | OpenAPI 3.1.0 document. |
| GET | `/api/schema/project.v3.json` | ProjectDoc v3 JSON Schema. |

### Tokens (admin)

| Method | Path | Result |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/tokens` | Body `{ "name", "scopes"?, "projectId"? }`. Returns `201` with `token` (`sfp_` + 32 hex characters). The token is shown only once. |
| GET | `/api/tokens` | `{ "tokens": [...] }` with `id`, `name`, `scopes`, `projectId`, `createdAt`, `revokedAt`, `lastUsedAt`. Never the token value. |
| DELETE | `/api/tokens/:id` | Revokes the token. Returns `{ "ok": true }`. |

### Projects

| Method | Path | Scope | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/projects` | read | `{ "projects": [{ id, title, version, updatedAt }] }`, most recently updated first. A project-limited token sees only its project. |
| POST | `/api/projects` | edit | Body `{ "id"?, "title"?, "doc"? }`. Returns `201 { id, title, version: 1, updatedAt }`. Without `doc`, the project gets an empty v3 document with one artboard, "Plan A". Without `id`, a UUID is made. `409` if the id exists. |
| GET | `/api/projects/:id` | read | `{ id, title, doc, version, updatedAt }`. `404` if missing. |
| PUT | `/api/projects/:id` | edit | Create or replace (upsert). Body `{ "doc", "title"? }`. `title` defaults to `doc.title`. The doc is validated (zod and the ProjectDoc semantic checks). Returns `{ ok, version, updatedAt }`. |
| PATCH | `/api/projects/:id` | edit | Rename. Body `{ "title", "baseVersion"? }`. The title inside the stored doc changes too. `404` if missing. |
| DELETE | `/api/projects/:id` | edit | Deletes the project and every R2 image under `images/<id>/`. Returns `{ ok, deletedImages }`. |

Validation errors return `400 { "error": "invalid_document", "issues": [{ code, severity, path, message }] }`.

### Versions and conflicts

- Every project has an integer `version`. It starts at 1 and goes up by 1 on each write (PUT, PATCH, commands).
- To avoid overwriting a newer change, send the version you read. Use `baseVersion` in the body, or the `If-Match: "<version>"` header. The body value wins when both are sent.
- If the stored version is different, the Worker returns `409 { "error": "version_conflict", "currentVersion": N }`. Read the project again, apply your change to the new doc, and retry.
- Without `baseVersion` or `If-Match`, the write does not check the version.

### Semantic routes

`POST /api/projects/:id/commands` (edit scope). Body: exactly one of `command` (one object) or `commands` (an array). Optional `dryRun: true` checks the change and saves nothing. Optional `baseVersion` or `If-Match`.

- A batch is all or nothing.
- Success: `{ ok: true, dryRun, version, updatedAt, result }`. `updatedAt` is not set on a dry run, and `version` is the current version.
- Failure: `400 { ok: false, error, issues? }`. Conflict: `409`.
- Command types: `set_title`, `add_artboard`, `update_artboard`, `duplicate_artboard`, `delete_artboard`, `add_room_rect`, `add_room_polygon`, `rename_room`, `move_room`, `set_wall_length`, `move_vertex`, `insert_vertex`, `delete_vertex`, `delete_rooms`, `cutout_rooms`, `merge_rooms`, `set_room_style`, `add_opening_on_wall`, `update_opening`, `delete_opening`, `add_furniture`, `update_furniture`, `reorder_furniture`, `duplicate_furniture`, `delete_furniture`.
- Most commands take an optional `artboardId`. The default is the first artboard.
- Example: `{"command":{"type":"add_room_rect","name":"Kitchen","xCm":0,"yCm":0,"widthCm":400,"heightCm":300}}`

`POST /api/projects/:id/query` (read scope). Body `{ "kind", "artboardId"? }`. Read-only.

- `summary`: `{ ok, summary }`.
- `validate`: `{ ok, valid, issues }`.
- `artboard`: `{ ok, artboard }`. The first artboard if `artboardId` is not sent.
- `rooms`: `{ ok, rooms }`.
- `walls`: `{ ok, walls }`. Each wall has `artboardId`, `roomId`, `roomName`, `edgeIndex`, `lengthCm`, `angleDeg`, `start`, `end` and `openingIds`.
- Unknown `kind`: `400`. Unknown `artboardId`: `404`.

`GET /api/projects/:id/render.svg?artboard=<id>` (read scope). Returns the artboard as `image/svg+xml`. Without `artboard`, the first artboard is used. `404` if the project or the artboard is missing.

### Images

| Method | Path | Scope | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/images/{projectId}/{imageId}` | read | Image bytes, sent with the Content-Type stored at upload. `404` if missing. |
| PUT | `/api/images/{projectId}/{imageId}` | edit | Stores the raw request body. The request Content-Type is kept (default `application/octet-stream`). Returns `{ ok, key }`. |
| DELETE | `/api/images/{projectId}/{imageId}` | edit | Deletes the image. Returns `{ ok: true }`. |

- Path segments use only letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`. A segment with `..` is refused with `400 { "error": "Invalid key" }`.
- The R2 object key is `images/<projectId>/<imageId>`.

### Error summary

Errors are JSON: `{ "error": "<message>" }`. `400` invalid JSON or input. `401` missing or wrong credentials. `403` scope too low or wrong project. `404` not found. `405` wrong method for the path. `409` version conflict or id already exists. Unknown path: `404`.

## ProjectDoc v3 example (minimal, valid)

This document passes the app schema (`parseProjectDoc`) and the JSON Schema at `/api/schema/project.v3.json`.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "id": "proj_1",
  "title": "Apartment 4B",
  "refImages": [],
  "artboards": [
    {
      "id": "plan_a",
      "name": "Plan A",
      "xCm": 0,
      "yCm": 0,
      "ceilingHeightCm": 250,
      "precisionCm": 1,
      "rooms": [
        {
          "id": "room_living",
          "name": "Living room",
          "vertices": [
            { "x": 0, "y": 0 },
            { "x": 400, "y": 0 },
            { "x": 400, "y": 300 },
            { "x": 0, "y": 300 }
          ]
        }
      ],
      "openings": [],
      "furniture": []
    }
  ]
}
```

Notes:

- `schemaVersion` must be the number `3`.
- `precisionCm` is `0.1`, `0.5` or `1`. Default `1`.
- `ceilingHeightCm` is greater than 0. Default `250` when omitted by the app schema.
- `wallThicknessCm` (0 to 50) is optional. Omitted means 10. `0` turns thick walls off.
- `wallKinds` is optional. It maps edge indices as strings (`"0"`, `"1"`, ...) to `"wall"` or `"fence"`; an edge with no entry is a normal wall. A fence is a low railing (for example a balcony parapet) about 100 cm high.
- Lengths are in cm. Angles are in degrees.

## MCP server (`POST /api/mcp`)

`POST /api/mcp` is a Model Context Protocol server. It uses the Streamable HTTP transport with JSON-RPC 2.0 messages. Send one JSON-RPC message per POST, with `Content-Type: application/json`. Send credentials as in the REST API (see Authentication). The route needs the `read` scope. Each tool checks its own scope, with the same rules as the REST routes.

Methods:

- `initialize`: returns `protocolVersion` `2025-03-26`, `capabilities: { tools: {} }` and `serverInfo` (`simple-floorplan`).
- `notifications/initialized`: a message without `id` (a notification). Returns `202` with an empty body.
- `ping`: returns `{}`.
- `tools/list`: returns the tools, each with `name`, `description` and `inputSchema`.
- `tools/call`: `params: { name, arguments }`.

Any other method returns `-32601`. A message without `id` never gets a JSON-RPC response body.

Tools:

| Tool | Scope | Arguments | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `list_projects` | read | none | Projects, most recently updated first. A project-limited token sees only its project. |
| `get_project` | read | `projectId` | Project `id`, `title`, `version`, `updatedAt` and the full ProjectDoc v3. |
| `create_project` | edit | `title?`, `id?`, `doc?` | The new project (version 1). Without `doc`, it has one empty artboard. |
| `query_project` | read | `projectId`, `kind` (`summary`, `validate`, `rooms`, `walls`, `artboard`), `artboardId?` | Read-only query result. |
| `run_commands` | edit | `projectId`, `command` or `commands`, `dryRun?`, `baseVersion?` | Same result as `POST /api/projects/:id/commands`. A batch is all or nothing. |
| `render_svg` | read | `projectId`, `artboardId?` | The artboard as SVG text. Default: the first artboard. |
| `delete_project` | edit | `projectId` | Deletes the project and its images. Cannot be undone. |

Errors:

- JSON-RPC errors: `-32700` parse error, `-32600` invalid request, `-32601` method not found, `-32602` invalid params (for example an unknown tool name, or `params.name` not a string).
- Tool errors return a normal result with `isError: true`. Examples: a missing `projectId`, a `400` or `409` from the command layer, or `Forbidden: this token cannot use <tool>` when the token scope is too low or the token is limited to another project.
- A successful tool result has `content` (one text item with the JSON result) and, for JSON results, `structuredContent`.

Example:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8788/api/mcp \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SFP_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```

## CLI (`cli/sfp.mjs`)

`cli/sfp.mjs` is a zero-dependency Node script (Node 22 or later). It wraps the REST API. Run it as `node cli/sfp.mjs <command>`, or as `npm run sfp -- <command>` (the `--` passes the arguments to the script).

Environment and flags:

- `SFP_URL`: API base URL. Default `http://localhost:8788`. Flag `--url <url>`.
- `SFP_TOKEN`: the master secret or a scoped token. Flag `--token <token>`.
- A token that starts with `sfp_` is sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Any other token is sent as `x-api-token`.
- Errors print `error: <message>` to stderr. The exit code is `1`. Success is `0`.

Commands:

| Command | Scope | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `projects` | read | List projects. |
| `create [title]` | edit | Create a project. |
| `pull <id> [out.json]` | read | Download the ProjectDoc. Writes a file, or prints to stdout. |
| `push <id> <file.json> [--base-version n]` | edit | Upload a ProjectDoc (`PUT`). `--base-version` sends `baseVersion`. |
| `query <id> <summary\|validate\|rooms\|walls\|artboard> [--artboard <aid>]` | read | Read-only query. |
| `exec <id> <jsonOrFile> [--dry-run] [--base-version n]` | edit | Run one command, or an array of commands. The argument is inline JSON, `@file.json`, or a path to a JSON file. |
| `render <id> [out.svg] [--artboard <aid>]` | read | Artboard SVG. Writes a file, or prints to stdout. |
| `delete <id>` | edit | Delete a project. |
| `help` | none | Show usage. |

Example:

```bash
export SFP_URL=http://localhost:8788
export SFP_TOKEN=sfp_...
npm run sfp -- projects
npm run sfp -- exec proj_1 '{"type":"add_room_rect","xCm":0,"yCm":0,"widthCm":400,"heightCm":300}' --dry-run
```

## Browser surface (in-page)

The app sets `window.sfp` (version `'3'`) when it starts. It edits the open project through the same command layer as the app. Every successful `exec` is one undo step. All return values are JSON-serializable. Units: cm and degrees.

- Read: `getDoc()` (deep copy of the ProjectDoc), `getUi()` (`mode`, `tool`, `activeArtboardId`, `selection`, `view`), `summarize()`, `validate()` (`{ ok, issues }`).
- Edit: `exec(cmdOrCmds, { dryRun? })` returns `{ ok: true, result, dryRun }` or `{ ok: false, error, issues? }`. An array of commands is all-or-nothing. `dryRun(cmdOrCmds)` checks without changing anything. `undo()` and `redo()` return `true` when the project changed.
- UI: `setMode('plan' | 'design')`, `setTool(tool)`, `select(selection)`, `setActiveArtboard(id)`, `setView({ x, y, zoom })`, `fitView(artboardId?)`.
- Files: `loadProject(input)` (validates, then replaces the project and clears undo history; returns `{ ok, error?, issues? }`), `exportProject()` (JSON text), `exportSvg(artboardId?)` (`{ ok: true, svg, artboardId }`).
- Coordinates: `worldToScreen(xCm, yCm)` and `screenToWorld(clientX, clientY)` use the canvas box and the view. They return `null` when no canvas is on the page.
- Events: `subscribe(({ rev, doc }) => ...)` returns an unsubscribe function. The window also fires `sfp:change` with `detail: { rev }`.

Example: `window.sfp.exec({ type: 'add_room_rect', name: 'Kitchen', xCm: 0, yCm: 0, widthCm: 400, heightCm: 300 })`.

When the browser has WebMCP (`navigator.modelContext.registerTool`), the app registers these tools. Without WebMCP, nothing is registered.

- `sfp_get_project`: summary and UI state.
- `sfp_get_doc`: the full ProjectDoc.
- `sfp_validate`: validation issues.
- `sfp_exec`: `{ commands, dryRun? }`; `commands` is one command or an array.
- `sfp_undo`, `sfp_redo`.
- `sfp_set_ui`: `{ mode?, tool?, activeArtboardId?, selection?, view?, fit? }`.
- `sfp_load_project`: `{ project }`.
- `sfp_export_svg`: `{ artboardId? }`.

The REST API above is for stored projects (cloud sync). `window.sfp` is for the project open in the page.

The SVG plan marks its entities in the DOM:

- `data-entity`: `room`, `wall`, `opening` or `furniture`.
- `data-id`: the entity id. For a `wall`, `data-id` is the id of its room.
- `data-edge`: the wall edge index. Set on `wall` elements only.
- Also present: `data-room-id`, `data-opening-id`, `data-furniture-id`, and `data-wall="<roomId>:<edgeIndex>"` on walls.
- Each element has an `aria-label` with a readable name, for example `Wall 2 of Living room, 400 cm`.

Numeric values are edited in the side panels with number fields (position, size, rotation, ceiling height, and similar). Values use cm and degrees.

## Browser URL parameters

The app reads these query parameters when it starts (`src/shell/urlParams.ts`). Invalid values are ignored. Parsing never throws.

| Parameter | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `project` | a project id | Loads the project from the cloud API (`GET /api/projects/:id`) and replaces the open project. Needs cloud access (see Authentication). A load error shows a message. |
| `mode` | `plan`, `design` | Sets the mode. |
| `tool` | `select`, `rect`, `pen`, `cutout`, `artboard`, `tape` | Sets the active tool. |
| `artboard` | an artboard id | Makes that artboard active, if it exists in the open project. |
| `nosw` | `1` or `true` | Unregisters every service worker before the app starts, so a stale PWA cache cannot serve an old build. |

Example: `https://<host>/?project=proj_1&mode=design&tool=tape&artboard=plan_a`

## Copy and paste actions (in-page UI)

- **Copy JSON**: copies the open project to the clipboard as JSON text. It is a toolbar button (`aria-label="Copy JSON"`), and it is also in the More menu.
- **Paste JSON**: opens a dialog (`aria-label="Paste JSON"`) where you paste project JSON. It is also in the More menu.
- **Copy SVG**: in the artboard inspector (`aria-label="Copy SVG"`), copies the SVG of that artboard to the clipboard.

## Not in this version

These are not implemented. Do not call them:

- `/snapshot`, `/items`, `/measurements`, `/events`, `/share`
- The `.sfp` text DSL, DXF export, the stdio MCP wrapper
- PlanDoc v1 and its `schemaVersion` 1 format
- `x-passcode`

## For AI agents: suggested order

1. Read `/api/schema/project.v3.json` to learn the document shape.
2. Read `/api/openapi.json` for the endpoint list.
3. Get credentials. Use the master secret, or ask an admin to create a scoped token with `POST /api/tokens`. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (or `x-api-token: <secret>`).
4. Call `GET /api/projects` to list projects and their `version` values.
5. Read with `POST /api/projects/:id/query` (for example `{"kind":"summary"}`), or with `GET /api/projects/:id`.
6. Change a project with `POST /api/projects/:id/commands`. Send `dryRun: true` first. Then send the same body without `dryRun`, with `baseVersion` set to the version you read.
7. To replace the whole document instead, read the project, change `doc`, and send it back with `PUT /api/projects/:id`, the same `title` and `baseVersion`.
8. On `409 version_conflict`, read the project again and retry.
